passages.title: Questions 111–120
passages.body: It is increasingly (111) _____ that learning levels within many countries are highly unequal. This (112) _____ be happening because of institutional features of school systems, such as early streaming, regional diversity (113) _____ expenditure or political engagement, (114) _____ access to education, and non-equitable access to different types of providers. Among the developed countries, (115) _____ with more equal learning outcomes (116) _____ have better average learning outcomes, (117) _____ that appropriate interventions in the education sector may have positive effects on both equality and the quality of education. Economic inequality is associated with the distribution of (118) _____ skills among adults, although the direction of causation is unclear. Arguably, (119) _____ society will ever reach total equality in the learning outcomes of every individual. (120) _____ in learning outcomes may depend on individual ability and motivation, as well as the type of background one comes from and the types of resources one has access to.
passages.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best replaces the underlined word in the context of the sentence.

The opposing political parties nevertheless took a __bilateral__ position in the national interest.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits the sense.
Step 1: Parties that are normally opposed but agree on one national issue take a 'bipartisan' (two-party) position.
Step 2: 'Bilateral' means between two countries, so it does not fit.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best replaces the underlined word in the context of the sentence.

Although she had sampled food from all the restaurants in the food court, she remained __indefinite__ towards the culinary fare on offer.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Match the meaning of the sentence.
Step 1: Having sampled all the food, she remained unmoved by it, i.e. indifferent.
Step 2: 'Indefinite' means unclear and does not fit.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best replaces the underlined word in the context of the sentence.

The attitude of the whalers was marked by __antipathy__ towards the marine life they had to encounter.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antipathy = strong dislike or hostility.
Step 1: Whalers hunt marine animals, so their attitude is one of hostility. Sympathy and empathy are the opposite.
Step 2: 'Animus' (hostile feeling) is the closest in meaning; 'indifference' lacks the hostility that the word 'antipathy' carries.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best replaces the underlined word in the context of the sentence.

The family was rendered __diligent__ due to the crash in the share market.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Confusable words.
Step 1: Indigent = poor. After a share-market crash a family is rendered poor, i.e. indigent.
Step 2: Diligent means hard-working, which does not fit.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best replaces the underlined word in the context of the sentence.

He had cultivated such great temperance in his personality that he was __impassioned__ in his dealing with the vicissitudes of life.
questions.explanation:
Concept: The sentence shows temperance (self-control).
Step 1: A person with temperance is not carried away by emotion in the ups and downs of life, so 'dispassionate' fits.
Step 2: 'Impassioned' means full of strong emotion, the opposite.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best replaces the underlined word in the context of the sentence.

The document was discerned to be a __postscript__, where clearly an earlier manuscript had been replaced by a new one.
questions.explanation:
Concept: A palimpsest is a manuscript on which the original writing has been erased and written over.
Step 1: The sentence says an earlier manuscript was replaced by a new one.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best replaces the underlined word in the context of the sentence.

He was accused of __simulism__ for having copied from someone else without due acknowledgement.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Copying without acknowledgement is plagiarism.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best replaces the underlined word in the context of the sentence.

The domineering manager behaved in a __paternal__ manner with his subordinates, not allowing them to decide for themselves.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Paternalistic = treating others like children by controlling them 'for their good'.
Step 1: The manager did not let subordinates decide, so 'paternalistic' fits better than 'paternal'.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best replaces the underlined word in the context of the sentence.

Much to their disappointment, the team leader spared no more than a __reflective__ glance at the draft plan drawn up by his team.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Perfunctory = done with little effort or interest.
Step 1: A team leader who spares no more than a quick glance gives a perfunctory glance.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best replaces the underlined word in the context of the sentence.

Her actions were considered __salutary__ because they were done without good reason or cause.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Gratuitous = done without good reason.
Step 1: 'Done without good reason or cause' defines gratuitous. Salutary means beneficial.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__In his well-recognised stentorian yet amused voice__ (a) __the principal demanded an unique excuse__ (b) __from the student hauled up for alleged minor misdemeanour.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use 'a' before a consonant sound.
Step 1: 'unique' begins with the sound 'yoo' (a consonant sound), so it should be 'a unique excuse'.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__The visiting school children__ (a) __went around the lake__ (b) __during trip to the famous lake city.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Nouns need an article.
Step 1: 'during trip' should be 'during the trip' or 'during a trip'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__The unfair distribution__ (a) __of assets among the family members__ (b) __angered the more hardworking members of the familyowned firm.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Check each part.
Step 1: 'The unfair distribution of assets among the family members angered the more hardworking members of the family-owned firm' is grammatically correct.
Answer: (d) No error.
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__Given the nature of the problem__ (a) __it was not unnatural for there to be__ (b) __bad blood among the two of them.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: 'Between' is used for two; 'among' for more than two.
Step 1: 'The two of them' are two persons, so 'bad blood between the two of them'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__He emphasised the need for__ (a) __strict discipline and compliance__ (b) __among the newly-appointed staff.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Check the sentence for mistakes.
Step 1: 'emphasised the need for strict discipline and compliance among the newly-appointed staff' is correct.
Answer: (d) No error.
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__The officer marvelled__ (a) __at the low attendance__ (b) __remarking on the presence of less than twenty people at work.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Fewer is used with countable nouns.
Step 1: 'People' are countable, so it should be 'fewer than twenty people'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__The entire attention of the visiting__ (a) __dignitaries centred around__ (b) __the craftwork on display.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Attention centres on something, not around it.
Step 1: The correct phrase is 'centred on' (or 'centred upon').
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__A group of wayfaring tourists__ (a) __who had trudged for hundreds of kilometres__ (b) __has finally arrived at the destination.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Subject-verb agreement.
Step 1: The subject is 'a group' (singular), so 'has arrived' is correct.
Answer: (d) No error.
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__The tumult among the gathered spectators__ (a) __rose to a crescendo__ (b) __upon the arrival of their most favourite superstar.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Do not use double superlatives.
Step 1: 'Favourite' already means most liked; 'most favourite' is wrong.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__The listings on the menu that had been proffered by him__ (a) __were selected after meticulous care__ (b) __and discernment with regard to taste and preference.__ (c)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Check the sentence.
Step 1: 'The listings ... were selected after meticulous care and discernment' is correct (listings is plural; 'were' agrees).
Answer: (d) No error.
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word to fill the blank.

Not ______ metal is necessarily solid in its natural state.
questions.explanation:
Concept: 'Not every' is used with a singular noun.
Step 1: 'metal' is singular, so 'Not every metal is solid' is correct. 'All' would need 'metals'.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word to fill the blank.

The reminder has gone out on ______ occasions, requiring personnel to complete their personal files.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Match the sense.
Step 1: 'on several occasions' means more than once, which suits a repeated reminder.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word to fill the blank.

It is important for people to work ______ their co-workers in the office to ensure maximum productivity.
questions.explanation:
Concept: 'Work with' = work together.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word to fill the blank.

You can choose ______ shirt you like from the collection available in the shop.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Whichever is used when choosing from a known set.
Step 1: The shirts come from the 'collection available in the shop', a limited set, so 'whichever'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word to fill the blank.

Depending on your preference, you can choose to complete either or ______ courses being offered by the university.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Fixed phrase 'either or both'.
Step 1: 'you can choose to complete either or both courses' makes sense.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Identify the sentences in which the underlined word has been used correctly.

Words: Dairy, Dreary, Diary
1. She quietly stored all her sacred memories in her private __dairy__.
2. The proceedings of the meeting went on and on and were quite __dreary__.
3. They always bought their milk products from the local __diary__.
In which of the sentences given above has/have the words been used correctly ?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Dairy = milk products; dreary = dull; diary = personal journal.
Step 1: 1 should be 'diary'. 2 'dreary' is correct. 3 should be 'dairy'.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Identify the sentences in which the underlined word has been used correctly.

Words: Braid, Beard, Brood
1. The engineers were asked to __braid__ the river by converting it into single body with the aid of an artificial dam.
2. Wise men, they say, often sport a __beard__.
3. Among certain avian species the males are known to __brood__ the eggs laid by females.
In which of the sentences given above has/have the words been used correctly ?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Braid = weave; beard = facial hair; brood = sit on eggs.
Step 1: 1 should be 'brace/block' not 'braid' (wrong). 2 'beard' is correct. 3 'brood the eggs' is correct.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Identify the sentences in which the underlined word has been used correctly.

Words: Lesion, Legion, Lesson
1. The scan of the affected area indicated the presence of a life-threatening __lesion__.
2. He had a __legion__ of followers who hung on to his every word.
3. It is important to __lesson__ the burden of others as we venture through life.
In which of the sentences given above has/have the words been used correctly ?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Lesion = wound or damaged tissue; legion = large group; lesson = teaching; lessen = reduce.
Step 1: 1 is correct. 2 is correct. 3 should be 'lessen the burden'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Identify the sentences in which the underlined word has been used correctly.

Words: Depose, Deplore, Deport
1. The director asked the actor to __depose__ himself and instead act naturally.
2. The people are enthusiastically declaring that they __deplore__ the salutary impact of the decisions taken by the administration.
3. Under extreme circumstances, the government can __deport__ someone from a country.
In which of the sentences given above has/have the words been used correctly ?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Depose = remove from power; deplore = strongly disapprove; deport = send out of a country.
Step 1: 1 is wrong ('compose' is meant). 2 is wrong ('welcome/applaud' is meant). 3 is correct.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Identify the sentences in which the underlined word has been used correctly.

Words: Bate, Bait, Bade
1. Those who had gathered for the unveiling were asked to __bate__ their curiosity.
2. They set the __bait__ to capture the leopard for tagging.
3. He reluctantly __bade__ goodbye to his belongings.
In which of the sentences given above has/have the words been used correctly ?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Bate = lessen or restrain (as in 'bated breath'); bait = lure; bade = past tense of bid.
Step 1: 1 'bate their curiosity' is not a natural use. 2 'bait' is correct. 3 'bade goodbye' is correct.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the meaning of the idiom or proverb.

Someone's ears are flapping
questions.opt_a: Someone in a state of intense agitation
questions.opt_b: Someone in a state of heightened excitement
questions.opt_c: Someone desperate to eavesdrop on a conversation
questions.opt_d: Someone embarrassed at being caught in the act of lying
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: Someone whose ears are flapping is trying hard to listen in to a conversation.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the meaning of the idiom or proverb.

Twist of the knife
questions.opt_a: Slicing through the difficulties that one faces in life
questions.opt_b: To accept defeat in the face of an enemy
questions.opt_c: The last thrust of a difficult operation
questions.opt_d: To make someone who is already feeling bad, feel worse with one's words or actions
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: A twist of the knife is an action or remark that makes a bad situation worse for someone.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the meaning of the idiom or proverb.

Blow your own trumpet
questions.opt_b: All sound and fury, signifying nothing
questions.opt_c: Excessively boastful of one's own achievements
questions.opt_d: Be scathing in one's criticism of others
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: To blow your own trumpet is to boast about your achievements.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the meaning of the idiom or proverb.

Get under someone's skin
questions.opt_a: To fall intensely in love with someone
questions.opt_b: To cause intense liking in someone
questions.opt_d: To annoy or irritate someone intensely
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: Someone who gets under your skin irritates you deeply.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the meaning of the idiom or proverb.

Many hands make light work
questions.opt_a: Many people working together can light a new path
questions.opt_b: Many people helping can help accomplish a task quickly
questions.opt_c: Many people working together can make work non-serious
questions.opt_d: Workers light up the work they undertake
questions.explanation:
Concept: Proverb.
Step 1: Many people sharing the work get it done easily and fast.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the meaning of the idiom or proverb.

A bird in hand is worth two in the bush
questions.opt_a: What's hidden is always a matter of speculation
questions.opt_b: What we have is always more valuable that what we have a chance of getting
questions.opt_c: A gift is always better kept close to oneself
questions.opt_d: What can happen is always better than what has happened
questions.explanation:
Concept: Proverb.
Step 1: What you already have is worth more than something you may get.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the meaning of the idiom or proverb.

Make heavy weather
questions.opt_c: To complain about wet and rainy conditions
questions.opt_d: Unnecessarily create difficulty in dealing with a task
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: To make heavy weather of something is to find it more difficult than it needs to be.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the meaning of the idiom or proverb.

Sweep under the carpet
questions.opt_c: Keep a problem under wraps in the hope that it will be forgotten
questions.opt_d: Do a quick clean up job
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: Sweeping something under the carpet means hiding a problem hoping it is forgotten.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the meaning of the idiom or proverb.

A purple patch
questions.opt_b: The final bloom of the season
questions.opt_c: A great run of luck or success or form
questions.opt_d: A bodily discolouration related to heredity
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: A purple patch is a period of great success or good form.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the meaning of the idiom or proverb.

Put out to pasture
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: Old horses are put out to pasture; so a person is retired or made redundant.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question:
Directions: Choose how the second sentence is related to the first.

S1: Failure is the stepping stone to success.
S2: Successive failures are not however successive stepping stones to success.
The second sentence :
questions.opt_a: contradicts the wisdom of the first
questions.opt_b: contrasts the wisdom of the first
questions.opt_c: confirms the wisdom of the first
questions.opt_d: qualifies the wisdom of the first
questions.explanation:
Concept: 'Not however' signals a limit.
Step 1: S1 says failure leads to success. S2 says repeated failures are not automatically stepping stones, so it limits (qualifies) S1.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question:
Directions: Choose how the second sentence is related to the first.

S1: All human beings are created equal in every respect.
S2: Some people are more equal than others.
The second sentence :
questions.explanation:
Concept: Contradiction.
Step 1: S1 says all are equal; S2 says some are more equal than others, which denies S1.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question:
Directions: Choose how the second sentence is related to the first.

S1: The origin of the universe has been traced to the Big Bang.
S2: There can be no knowledge of what existed before the Big Bang.
The second sentence :
questions.opt_a: contradicts the assertion made in the first
questions.opt_b: explains the basis behind the first
questions.opt_c: establishes limits on the assertion made in the first
questions.opt_d: confirms the assertion made in the first
questions.explanation:
Concept: Setting limits.
Step 1: S1 traces the origin to the Big Bang; S2 says nothing can be known before it. S2 limits how far S1's claim can go.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question:
Directions: Choose how the second sentence is related to the first.

S1: The highest clouds in the skies are the most fascinating.
S2: We are most attracted to those things that are most out of our reach.
The second sentence :
questions.opt_a: reiterates the axiom stated in the first
questions.opt_b: annuls the axiom stated in the first
questions.opt_c: contradicts the axiom stated in the first
questions.opt_d: contrasts the assertion made in the first
questions.explanation:
Concept: Reiterates = says the same idea again in other words.
Step 1: Both sentences say that the most distant things attract us most.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question:
Directions: Choose how the second sentence is related to the first.

S1: A four-stroke engine is more efficient than a two-stroke engine.
S2: The two-stroke engine has been phased out to protect the environment.
The second sentence :
questions.explanation:
Concept: Correlates = related to.
Step 1: S1 says the four-stroke engine is more efficient (cleaner). S2 says the two-stroke is phased out for the environment. The second is related to, and consistent with, the first, but does not state the same claim.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question:
Directions: Choose how the second sentence is related to the first.

S1: Bottled water is safer than tap water.
S2: In many countries tap water is fed to babies.
The second sentence :
questions.opt_d: is an extension of the first
questions.explanation:
Concept: Contrast.
Step 1: S1 says bottled water is safer; S2 says tap water is given to babies, which points the other way.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question:
Directions: Choose how the second sentence is related to the first.

S1: The peacock is India's national bird.
S2: The Great Indian Bustard is the state bird of Rajasthan.
The second sentence :
questions.opt_a: provides additional information to what is contained in the first
questions.opt_b: provides contradictory information to what is contained in the first
questions.opt_c: provides less information than what is contained in the first
questions.opt_d: provides escalatory information to what is contained in the first
questions.explanation:
Concept: Additional information.
Step 1: Both sentences are about birds; S2 adds a different fact.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2025 English set A (set code ANFB-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question:
Directions: Choose how the second sentence is related to the first.

S1: Field games are generally more popular than individual sports.
S2: Across the world tennis is more popular than hockey.
The second sentence :
questions.explanation:
Concept: General rule vs exception.
Step 1: S1 says field games (like hockey) are generally more popular than individual sports. S2 says tennis (individual) is more popular than hockey (field), which stands in contrast to the general rule without fully denying it.
Answer: (c).

questions.opt_d: The news of the earthquake illicited a massive outpouring of help for the victims.
